mira: quick FYI — after the 03:00 canary we saw a 95th latency jump for short responses when prefix cache hit > 60%. not huge p95 but consistent on the canary hosts.

sam: can you paste the perf trace? which kernel chosen for the short path?

mira: pasted below. kernel selector picks the small-seq path (kern_v2_small) when virt_len < 32, but the planner is still batching across both cache-hit and cache-miss requests so the GPU kernel switch frequency increased.

mira: ```
# simplified trace
[2026-03-16T03:12:04Z] req A (hit) virt_len=8 -> packed into microbatch 1 -> kern_v2_small
[2026-03-16T03:12:04Z] req B (miss) virt_len=120 -> held for batching -> kern_v2_long
[2026-03-16T03:12:04Z] batch flush -> mixed kernels -> extra memcpy / kernel-sync
p95 increased from 32ms -> 52ms
```

kai: mixing small/long kernels in same launch is what bites us — kernel-switch overhead + extra memory ops. Did we see any change in token-budget/epoching config after canary? maybe continuous-batcher opened wider windows.

mira: yes, batch_window_ms bumped from 8 -> 20 in canary to improve throughput. that increased chance of mixing hits/misses. also KV cache hit packing currently doesn't pre-split by virt_len class.

anya: idea: try 'epoching' the queue by cache-hit status + virt_len bucket. i.e., maintain two short-lived epochs: HIT/SHORT and MISS/LONG; the scheduler prefers to drain hits into small-kernel-only batches and misses into long-kernel batches. keeps kernel selection stable.

sam: sounds good. downside: could increase latency for rare types (e.g., a hit that waits for short-epoch window). What's the plan for token-budget targets?

mira: propose aggressive token-budget target for HIT/SHORT of 32 tokens and tight max-delay 6ms. for MISS/LONG keep existing 120 token target and 20ms delay. Both epochs live for ~10ms before cross-epoch bleed allowed.

kai: perf-bot: run a micro-canary with these params on 5 hosts with a synthetic mix: 70% cached short prompts (avg virt_len 10), 30% cold long prompts (avg virt_len 150). collect p50/p95/p99 and kernel-switch counts.

perf-bot: acknowledged. scheduling run id=run-20260316-1

mira: also add a quick profiler hook to count kernel_invoke per-batch and memcpy bytes. grep for PACKER:kernel_switch in logs.

sam: if this reduces kernel-switches and p95, we should consider making epoching dynamic: if hit fraction > X then enable hit-epoch, else disabled. keep it opt-in for canary first.

anya: +1. also add a safety fallback: if epoching causes starvation (requests waited > 100ms) immediately drain.

kai: i'll spin up the canary job. timeline: run now, check results in 30m, if p95 improves we can A/B config to 50% traffic.

mira: thanks. I'll attach sample traces and a small test harness to reproduce locally.

sam: one more ask: capture kernel selection jitter metric (distinct kernel ids per rolling-second). that'll show instability.

mira: good call. I'll add a dashboard tile.

anya: OK team, running with those knobs. ping if you see regressions in other SLOs. :rocket:
